resources-prompts.summary: Resources are application-driven context addressed by URIs; prompts are user-controlled message templates; completion helps users fill in prompt and template arguments. Around them sit the list utilities every primitive shares: opaque-cursor pagination and the `ttlMs`/`cacheScope` caching hints added in 2026-07-28. Know the control model, the exact error codes, and how caching interacts with notifications and authorization.
points: Control model: tools are model-controlled, resources are application-driven (the host decides what to attach), prompts are user-controlled (the user picks them, often as slash commands). User-controlled is about who triggers a prompt; the server writes its content.

Resources have a unique RFC 3986 URI, a `name`, and optional `title`, `description`, `mimeType`, `size` and icons. `resources/read` returns `contents` items with `uri`, `mimeType` and either `text` or base64 `blob`, and MAY return several items (for example a directory's files).

Resource templates (`resources/templates/list`) use RFC 6570 URI templates such as `users://{id}/profile` to expose families of resources without enumerating them. `{var}` percent-encodes `/`; `{+var}` keeps it, which suits multi-segment paths.

Use `https://` only when the client can fetch the resource directly; otherwise use another scheme or a custom one that follows RFC 3986. `file://` resources need not map to a real filesystem, and servers MAY use XDG types like `inode/directory`.

Annotations on resources, templates and content blocks: `audience` (`user` and/or `assistant`), `priority` (0.0 to 1.0, 1 = effectively required) and `lastModified` (ISO 8601). They are hints for filtering, prioritising and sorting, not access control.

Resource not found is `-32602` in 2026-07-28 (was `-32002`; clients SHOULD still accept it). Servers MUST NOT return an empty `contents` array for a missing resource, and SHOULD use `-32603` for internal errors. Servers MUST validate URIs and sanitise `file://` paths against traversal.

A tool can return a `resource_link` (a pointer the client may read later, not necessarily in `resources/list`) or an embedded `resource` (contents inline). Link large or optional content; embed small content that is needed right away.

Per-resource change notifications in 2026-07-28: open `subscriptions/listen` with URIs in `resourceSubscriptions` (server capability `resources.subscribe`) and receive `notifications/resources/updated`. This replaces `resources/subscribe` from 2025-11-25. `list_changed` notifications only signal membership changes.

Prompts: `prompts/list` returns name, title, description and `arguments` (name, title, description, required). `prompts/get` returns `messages` with role `user` or `assistant` and one content block each (text, image, audio, resource link or embedded resource). Missing required arguments or an unknown name give `-32602`.

`completion/complete` takes a `ref` (`ref/prompt` by name or `ref/resource` by URI or template), the `argument` being typed and `context.arguments` with earlier choices. Results hold up to 100 `values`, an optional `total` and `hasMore`. The server declares `completions`; servers SHOULD rank and rate limit, clients SHOULD debounce.

Pagination for `tools/list`, `prompts/list`, `resources/list` and `resources/templates/list` uses an opaque `cursor`/`nextCursor`; the page size is the server's choice; a missing `nextCursor` ends the list, while an empty string is a valid cursor. Invalid cursors SHOULD get `-32602`.

Caching: `server/discover`, the four list methods and `resources/read` MUST carry `ttlMs` (>= 0) and `cacheScope` (`public` or `private`). The key is the method plus the relevant parameters; `input_required` results and MRTR retries are never cached; a missing or negative TTL means stale; notifications invalidate fresh entries; private caches MUST NOT cross authorization contexts.
traps: Calling `resources/subscribe` on a 2026-07-28 server: subscriptions moved to `subscriptions/listen` with `resourceSubscriptions`.
Returning or checking for an empty `contents` array to mean not found; use `-32602` (accept `-32002` from older servers).
Treating `""` as the end of pagination, or parsing cursors as offsets; cursors are opaque and only a missing `nextCursor` ends the list.
Marking per-user list or read results `cacheScope: "public"`: shared gateways may serve them to other users, and `cacheScope` never replaces access control.
Using `ttlMs` as a polling interval; it is a freshness hint checked on access, and any polling MUST use jitter and backoff.
Assuming read-only data must be a resource: if the model has to decide when to fetch it, a read-only tool is the reliable choice.
Treating prompt inputs as trusted because prompts are user-controlled; implementations MUST validate prompt inputs and outputs against injection and unauthorized access.
